title: The Circulatory System
seo_title: Year 6 Science: The Circulatory System Worksheets (Heart, Blood and Pulse Rate)
standard_text: Identify and name the main parts of the human circulatory system, and describe the functions of the heart, blood vessels and blood.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on the circulatory system: the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries, blood cells, the double loop and pulse rate investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The heart pumps blood round the body.
key_sub: Arteries away, veins back; blood carries oxygen from the lungs to the cells.
body_html:
How to think about it

The heart pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of the body.

  • Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back; capillaries let oxygen and nutrients reach the cells.
  • Double loop: body → heart → lungs (pick up oxygen) → heart → body.
  • Blood: red blood cells carry oxygen, white blood cells fight germs, platelets clot, plasma carries nutrients and water.
  • Pulse rate (beats per minute) = beats counted × how many of those time periods fit in 60 seconds.
Example

20 beats in 15 seconds. Pulse rate?

60 ÷ 15 = 4

20 × 4

Answer: 80 beats per minute

Example

Blood leaves the lungs. Next?

Lungs → left side of heart

Answer: the heart, then the body

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up arteries and veins.
  • Forgetting to scale up: 20 beats in 15 seconds is not 20 per minute.
  • Thinking blood goes from the body straight back to the body without the lungs.

faq.q: What does the circulatory system do?
faq.a: It moves blood around the body. Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to the cells and takes away waste such as carbon dioxide.

faq.q: What is the difference between arteries and veins?
faq.a: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins carry blood back to the heart. Tiny capillaries join them.

faq.q: How do you work out a pulse rate?
faq.a: Count the beats for a set time, such as 15 seconds, then multiply to find the beats in 60 seconds. For 15 seconds, multiply by 4.
